newsitem.title: Turkmenistan: Ex-Soviet states owe Turkmenistan $1.76 bln-agency.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet states owe Turkmenistan $1.76 bln-agency.

text.p: Republics of the former Soviet Soviet Union owe Turkmenistan $1.76 billion, the official Turkmen Press news agency said on Tuesday.
The agency said the figure for the debt -- mostly for supplies of Turkmen natural gas -- was released on Monday during a cabinet meeting headed by President Saparmurat Niyazov.

"The money to be received for supplies of Turkmen natural gas has been included in the expenses of this year's state budget, and its absence will create difficulties for the Turkmen economy," the agency quoted Niyazov as saying.

Ukraine is Turkmenistan's biggest debtor, owing the Central Asian state over $1 billion. The sum includes debts for the first three months of this year and for 1996 worth $302.5 million, as well as $780.6 million for 1993-1995.

The agency said Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma's visit to Turkmenistan scheduled for May 5-6 had been postponed at the request of the Turkmen side because Ukraine "was not ready to discuss payments of its debts and conclude contracts on concrete conditions of payments for supplies to be made in 1997".

Another former Soviet republic -- Georgia -- owes Turkmenistan $22.2 million for natural gas supplies in 1996 and in the first quarter of this year, while its debts for 1993-1995 amount to $442.7 million.
Turkmen Press said Niyazov had written to Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze asking him to settle his country's debts.
The agency said Russia, whose pipelines are used by Turkmenistan to export its gas to countries of the former Soviet Union and Europe, owed another $71 million for natural gas.

It also said Russia's Vneshekonombank -- the successor of the Soviet Union's Bank for Foreign Economic Activity -- owed Turkmen citizens $107.2 million. The money was frozen on the bank's accounts after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
